cell.label: Suspected TMJ disorder: Pain in the area of the TMJ, difficulty chewing, joint clicking or popping, and chronic undifferentiated headache.
Consider urgent treatment with muscle relaxants, oral or IV benzodiazepines.
Proceed immediately to reduction of the dislocated joint, consider IV pain control and/or IV benzodiazepines prior to procedure.
Point tenderness suggestive of a myofascial trigger point?
Consider intramuscular trigger point injection with local anesthetic.
Dental pathology (caries, dental abscess, etc.) on exam?
Infectious etiology causing pain? (Otitis media, otitis externa, parotitis, mastoiditis, and herpes zoster, etc.)
Signs or symptoms suggestive of other pathology?

Recommend self-care for TMJ disorders: rest the masticatory muscles with a soft diet, use NSAIDs or acetaminophen for pain, apply moist heat to the joint for muscle relaxation, and reduce stress and anxiety. Consider referral for other noninvasive therapies such as physical therapy modalities, acupuncture, massage, hypnosis, or stress management. Consider prescription for muscle relaxants, anxiolytics, tri-cyclic antidepressants.
Evaluate and treat the other condition
